key_insight: The paper shows that standard image Vision Transformers can learn strong video representations without specialized 3D models. By turning videos into "super images" and using masked self-supervision, VideoMSN efficiently captures spatio-temporal structure from unlabeled video.
problem_solved: It addresses the high cost and complexity of learning video representations with unlabeled data, which often requires heavy 3D architectures or reconstruction-based autoencoders.
method: Convert a video into a "super image" by arranging sampled frames into a grid representation.
Create two complementary views: one with spatial patch masking and another with temporal masking to encourage learning of both appearance and motion.
Train a Masked Siamese Network using standard image ViTs, avoiding expensive video-specific backbones.
Learn self-supervised spatio-temporal features from unlabeled videos efficiently.
impact: This makes video self-supervised learning more practical, cheaper, and easier to scale using existing image-classifier architectures. For practitioners, it lowers the barrier to building strong video representations without large computational overhead.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing video frames transformed into a super image

paper_title: Image Classifiers are Efficient Self-Supervised Video Representation Learners
paper_authors: Owais Iqbal, Sudipta Sarkar, Shyam Marjit, Omprakash Chakraborty, Anirban Chakraborty
